summary.oneLiner: G M Polyplast Limited is a single-segment Indian plastics converter manufacturing plastic sheets and granules (HIPS, ABS, PET, PP and HDPE), with FY2025-26 revenue from operations of Rs. 102.99 crore.
summary.business: G M Polyplast Limited operates in a single reportable business segment, namely the manufacture of plastic sheets and granules (HIPS, ABS, PET, PP and HDPE). Management describes the business as built on quality, operational excellence and customer satisfaction, and positions it to serve emerging opportunities in key sectors such as pharmaceuticals, packaging and interior solutions. During FY2025-26 the Company also promoted and incorporated Regranix Private Limited as a wholly-owned subsidiary, which had not commenced business operations as at March 31, 2026.

endMarkets: Pharmaceuticals|Packaging|Interior solutions|Exports (the Company recorded foreign exchange earnings during FY2025-26)

related.name: Regranix Private Limited
related.note: Wholly-owned subsidiary (CIN U2013MH2026PTC469366 per Form AOC-1; the Directors' Report prints it as U20131MH2026PTC469366), subsidiary since March 13, 2026. Form AOC-1 reports every financial line as 'Not Applicable' and records that Regranix commenced its business operations only during FY2026-27. A proposed related-party transaction places the Company's investment in Regranix - by way of subscription to equity shares, preference shares, debentures, bonds and/or other instruments, in one or more tranches, at arm's length - before members; the Audit Committee (a majority of Independent Directors) reviewed and approved it before the Board, and related parties abstain from voting under Regulation 23(4) of SEBI LODR. The stated rationale is to strengthen Regranix so it can expand its manufacturing capacity and emerge as a reliable, captive source of raw materials, reducing the Company's dependence on third-party suppliers and improving procurement certainty; investment is to be made tranche-wise, linked to Regranix's actual capital requirements, under Board monitoring.

D D & Associates, Chartered Accountants) reporting half-yearly to the Audit Committee.|Clean audit record: the Statutory Auditors' Report for the financial year contains no qualification, reservation, adverse remark or disclaimer.
currentContext.strategies: Continued emphasis on product innovation, capacity expansion and sustainable manufacturing practices, aimed at emerging opportunities in pharmaceuticals, packaging and interior solutions.|Build on the market position consolidated in recent years through focused strategies and agile execution, while continuing to invest in capacity and future growth.|Diversify the group through Regranix Private Limited, the wholly-owned subsidiary incorporated on March 13, 2026, described as reflecting a focus on long-term strategic growth and diversification.|Deepen relationships with strategic partners to support further diversification and market reach.|Fund growth conservatively: retain profits to build net worth and operate at a very low level of gearing while self-funding capital expenditure from operating cash.|Maintain a documented internal control framework with an annual business plan, quarterly revenue and capital-expenditure budgets and variance analysis, supported by independent half-yearly internal audit reporting to the Audit Committee.
currentContext.expansion: The MD&A frames FY2025-26 as a year in which the Company continued 'to invest in capacity and future growth', with strong operating cash generation enabling 'a significant step-up in capital expenditure' - gross Property, Plant & Equipment increased from Rs. 558.75 lakhs to Rs. 908.46 lakhs during the year - while cash and bank balances were simultaneously strengthened. Looking forward, management states that 'continued emphasis on product innovation, capacity expansion and sustainable manufacturing practices' positions the Company to capture emerging opportunities in pharmaceuticals, packaging and interior solutions, supported by expanding relationships with strategic partners. The only named new asset in the routed material is Regranix Private Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary incorporated on March 13, 2026 as part of the Company's long-term strategic growth and diversification, which had not commenced business operations as at March 31, 2026. On the energy side, the Directors' Report records that the Company 'has installed solar Panels at the Factory site' as part of its energy-conservation measures. No project names, commissioning dates, ramp timelines, plant locations or capex quantum for future projects are disclosed anywhere in the routed material, and the capital-commitments note states there were no capital commitments for the reporting period.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility tied to petrochemical feedstocks
risks.note: MD&A states that 'Volatility in raw material prices, closely linked to fluctuations in petrochemical feedstocks, continues to introduce uncertainty into cost structures and profitability', and repeats persistent raw-material price volatility under Risks and Concerns. Cost of materials consumed is by far the dominant cost line for a plastic sheets-and-granules converter, so feedstock swings pass straight through to margin.

risks.risk: Tightening plastic-waste environmental regulation and EPR compliance
risks.note: MD&A flags that 'Tightening environmental regulations around plastic waste management continue to demand higher investment in sustainable materials, waste recycling infrastructure and compliance mechanisms, which may elevate operational costs', and that compliance with mandatory Extended Producer Responsibility norms across the value chain 'remains an ongoing area for improvement'.

risks.risk: Regulatory uncertainty: single-use plastic bans, evolving Plastic Waste Management Rules and inconsistent enforcement
risks.note: The Company notes India has implemented bans on identified single-use plastics and continues to strengthen Plastic Waste Management Rules, while 'enforcement remains inconsistent in several regions' - creating both compliance-cost risk and an uneven competitive playing field.

risks.risk: Structural pressure to reduce plastic use / sustainability transition cost
risks.note: 'Growing public and governmental focus on reducing plastic use and increasing sustainability investment continues to create cost and compliance considerations for the industry' - a demand-side and capital-allocation risk to the whole plastics category the Company operates in.

risks.risk: Intense competition in a fragmented market limiting pricing power
risks.note: MD&A states 'Intense competition in a fragmented market continues to restrict pricing power for smaller participants', which is directly relevant to a company of this scale operating in a single reportable segment.

risks.risk: Trade uncertainty, protectionism in export markets and currency volatility
risks.note: 'Trade uncertainties, protectionist policies in key export markets and currency volatility pose ongoing risks to international growth ambitions'; Risks and Concerns adds that global trade uncertainties and supply-chain considerations 'continue to add financial and operational risk for manufacturers'. The Company recorded both foreign exchange earnings and larger foreign exchange outgo during the year, so it carries currency exposure on both sides.

The Company 'operates in a single reportable business segment, namely the manufacture of plastic sheets and granules (HIPS, ABS, PET, PP and HDPE)', so there is no segment diversification to absorb a shock to plastics demand, regulation or feedstock costs.

risks.risk: Infrastructure gaps and skilled-labour shortages constraining scaling
risks.note: MD&A notes 'Infrastructure gaps and shortages of skilled labour in certain regions continue to constrain scaling and technology adoption for smaller players' - a stated constraint on capacity expansion and technology absorption.
